slides.title: Chat beside the map
slides.html: OpenDefence Matrix puts your OpenDefence chat in a pane under the ATAK map. You read and write without leaving the map.

slides.title: Same chat as Element X
slides.html: OpenDefence Matrix is the same chat as the Element X app. People on either app talk in the same rooms.

slides.title: Where it opens
slides.html: The chat button at the top opens OpenDefence Matrix in place of ATAK's GeoChat. With OpenDefence Main, Chat at the bottom left opens it too, once you sign in.

slides.title: More than text
slides.html: A chat carries photos, videos, files, voice messages and polls as well as text. Photos are sent smaller, to save data.

slides.title: Share from the map
slides.html: You can send a point, route or drawing from the map to a chat. You can also put what others send on your own map.

slides.title: Kept private
slides.html: Rooms and direct chats made in OpenDefence Matrix are end-to-end encrypted, so only the people in them can read what is said. Message info says so, as here.

slides.title: No location in photos
slides.html: Photos and videos go without the location stored in the file. The attach panel says so before you send.

slides.title: Your position on messages
slides.html: Your position can go as the grid under your messages, only in encrypted chats. The pin by the message field turns it off.
